beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (bridges, railways, roads) and operating a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant.
Contracts are won through a government tender process: a client floats a tender, the company bids, and the lowest quote typically wins. A performance guarantee must be deposited before work begins.

Major clients include Western Railway, Central Railway, MCGM, MMRDA, and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation. Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book and 57% of fiscal 2018 revenue.
The company is focused on Mumbai and Maharashtra but is slowly consolidating its position within the state.
The company lists modern techniques (e.g., box pushing method) and state-of-the-art machinery at its Thane RMC plant as competitive strengths.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations declined from ₹90.21 crore in FY2015 to ₹60.53 crore in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over four years.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) was ₹9.29 crore in FY2018, up from ₹6.76 crore in FY2017 but below the ₹9.46 crore in FY2016.
Net profit after adjustments swung from ₹0.16 crore in FY2017 to ₹3.15 crore in FY2018, recovering from a trough but still below the ₹0.96 crore in FY2014.
Total assets have grown to ₹82.32 crore as of March 31, 2018, from ₹70.62 crore in FY2014, driven by an increase in short-term borrowings (₹35.37 crore in FY2018 vs ₹30.82 crore in FY2014).

Long-term borrowings are low at ₹1.33 crore, while short-term borrowings constitute the bulk of debt at ₹35.37 crore. The company also had ₹4.05 crore in unsecured loans repayable on demand as of FY2018.
The company reported negative cash flows in recent financial years; sustained negative cash flow could impact operations.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares — 90.949% of the pre-issue capital.
Other directors hold minimal shares: Bharat Kumar Parmar (300), Shree Prakash Singh (300), and Mukesh Pandey (300). Key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori and CS Mohit Soni.

Related-party transactions include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors (₹68.4 lakhs in FY2018), director remuneration (₹57.7 lakhs), and outstanding payables to related parties (₹324.3 lakhs as of March 31, 2018).
Two companies promoted by the promoter — Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited — have been struck off by the Registrar of Companies for non-operation.
No criminal cases have been filed against directors, and none are listed as willful defaulters by the RBI.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector in India is highly fragmented and working capital intensive, contributing ~8% to GDP. Government flagship programs like Smart Cities, AMRUT, and Make in India are key demand drivers.
FDI norms in 15 sectors including construction have been eased; India requires an estimated ₹50 trillion in infrastructure investment by 2022.
The logistics sector, closely tied to infrastructure, is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020.
Headwinds identified by the company include a slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.
Competition comes from both organized and unorganized players; the market is highly fragmented.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor and ready-mix concrete manufacturer, dependent on government tenders — especially from Indian Railways.
The SME IPO consists of 44,28,000 fresh equity shares; proceeds will primarily fund working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and general corporate purposes.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who A B Infrabuild is, what it does, and why it's raising money.

beats.beat: The issue comprises 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined. It is a fresh issue — no offer for sale component.
Net proceeds will be used primarily to meet working capital requirements (₹1,130 lakhs) and for general corporate purposes (amount not disclosed).
Lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the project, and no monitoring agency has been appointed — fund deployment will be monitored by the Audit Committee.

offer.heading: The offer and its objects
offer.purpose: Detail the issue structure, use of proceeds, and lead manager.

beats.beat: Revenue concentration on one customer: Indian Railways (via Western Railway, Central Railway, MRVCL) contributed 57% of revenue in fiscal 2018 and 52% of the order book. Loss of this customer would severely impact revenue.
Dependence on winning government tenders is a key risk; the company's revenues largely depend on bid acceptance. If bids fail, financial condition could be materially affected.
Negative cash flows in recent years and high short-term borrowings (₹35.37 crore) expose the company to liquidity stress. Unsecured loans of ₹4.05 crore are repayable on demand.
The company has not appointed an independent agency to appraise the use of funds, and no monitoring agency is in place — fund deployment is at management discretion (overseen by Audit Committee).

The issue price may not reflect the market price after listing; shares have been issued at a lower price in the last 12 months, and the DRHP warns that investors may not be able to sell at or above the issue price.
